theater: 葡萄牙與卡斯提爾戰線

battle.name: 半島戰爭
battle.theater: 葡萄牙與卡斯提爾戰線
battle.brief: 一八〇七年十月，法軍越過比斯開灣攻入葡萄牙，半島戰爭自此開打，至一八一四年土魯斯一役收兵。戰線在里斯本、卡斯提爾與巴斯克之間推移；卡面長槍已非制式兵器，方陣長矛在十八世紀便被燧發滑膛槍取代，留在軍中的只是榮譽與象徵，決定交火距離的是線列步兵的燧發火槍與承襲長矛方陣邏輯的拒止翼。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 法國方面，遠征伊比利亞的是拿破崙第一帝國的西班牙軍團。一八〇七年十月，朱諾率約二萬四千人自比斯開灣登陸，掃平葡萄牙，此後由普隆通、內伊、莫里耶、索爾特、馬塞納、儒爾當、克萊爾等將領輪流接手，指揮權自帝國中央與巴黎後勤總署逐步下放到軍團一級；一八〇九年索爾特第九軍團成為盤踞卡斯提爾的最大法軍集群，另有波蘭輕騎與法屬意大利籍士兵編入。佔領區的開支由巴黎的西班牙軍團總署直接向西班牙抽稅，遠征軍於是成了壓在自己佔領地上的吸血裝置。西班牙方面，王國在斐迪南七世被押往巴亞昂後由各地最高中央委員會主持，軍隊分為中央軍團、卡斯提爾軍團、安達盧西亞軍團與巴斯克軍團，作戰上服從中央命令，指揮卻極不統一；線列步兵以線列團為骨幹，民兵營與義勇軍補充兵力，軍紀與後勤長期吃緊。葡萄牙方面，葡軍在法軍佔領期間瓦解，一八〇九年初由貝雷斯福德在英軍顧問團協助下重建，混編英葡旅，兵力自不足一萬逐步壯大。英國方面，由威靈頓指揮的遠征軍自一八〇八年秋起投入，除英國皇家陸軍與海軍陸戰隊外，還有皇家騎砲兵、皇家工兵兵團與皇家後勤兵團，並以皇家海軍封鎖線維持比斯開灣與加的斯港的海上補給。西班牙全境的游擊隊則以地方營與游擊小隊自行編組，貫穿整場戰爭。
countriesEn: France fought through the Army of Spain, the Napoleonic expeditionary force in Iberia. In October 1807 Junot landed with roughly 24,000 men from the Bay of Biscay and swept through Portugal; command then passed in turn to Victor, Ney, Mortier, Soult, Masséna, Jourdan and Clausel, with authority drifting downward from the imperial centre and the Paris administrative office to the level of the army corps. From 1809 Soult's Ninth Corps became the largest French concentration in Castile, and Polish light cavalry and troops from French Italy were folded into the order of battle. The costs of the occupation were met by levies extracted from Spain itself through the Paris administration, so the expeditionary army ended up draining the very territory it held. In Spain, after Ferdinand VII was taken to Bayonne, the kingdom was governed by a series of Supreme Central Juntas. The field forces were split into the Army of the Centre, the Army of Castile, the Army of Andalusia and the Basque forces, nominally subordinate to the central junta but never genuinely unified in command. Line infantry rested on the regiments of the line, with militia battalions and volunteer formations filling out the ranks, while discipline and supply stayed chronically weak. Portugal's army dissolved during the French occupation and was rebuilt from early 1809 by Beresford with a British advisory corps, forming mixed brigades that grew from fewer than 10,000 men. Britain committed the expeditionary army under Wellington from the autumn of 1808, adding the Royal Horse Artillery, the Royal Engineers and the Royal Logistic Corps, while the Royal Navy kept the sea approaches to Biscay and Cádiz open. Partida bands across Spain organised themselves locally and threaded through the entire war.
people: 關鍵人物分屬三邊。朱諾是法軍入葡的先鋒，也是維梅羅一役的敗將；索爾特最擅長持久消耗，在安達盧西亞與卡斯提爾拖住聯軍近四年，維多利亞前夜仍是他主動迎戰；馬蒙在薩拉曼卡的失手，直接讓法軍北線的整條防線崩解。威靈頓自一八〇八年秋率遠征軍入境，先以一場維梅羅的模範撤退保住英軍，再以貝雷斯福德的葡軍縱隊作為左翼與前哨，逐步把守勢轉成反攻；其參謀長喬治·穆雷、工事官鮑威爾與騎兵指揮巴寧克等人，把聯軍的後勤與騎兵運作到足以支撐連續作戰的程度。英方另一個關鍵人物是摩爾，他在科魯尼以退為進，陣亡於撤退途中；巴林漢在巴達霍斯率縱隊強行攻城，捱過英軍歐洲戰史上最慘烈的一次縱隊攻擊。西班牙方面，卡斯塔尼奧斯在塞維亞集結軍隊、帕拉福克斯死守薩拉戈薩、奧唐奈拿下科魯尼與聖安東尼奧、拉羅馬納在梅諾卡島擊退法軍、埃斯帕特羅在西北戰線追擊法軍；五月二日至六日馬德里起義被鎮壓的消息傳遍各地，斐迪南七世與全國的信任幾近斷裂。游擊隊方面，埃斯波斯·伊·米納在納瓦拉與阿拉貢的山區經營游擊網，埃爾·恩佩西納多率數百人的游擊隊在瓜達拉哈拉一帶攔截法軍縱隊，情報與金屬都靠他們翻山送達。還要提的是拿破崙本人：他以帝國中心的視角遙控戰場，把西班牙視為牽制英國的次要戰區，這一輕敵最終成了整場戰爭的根源。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities fall into three camps. Junot was the spearhead of the French invasion of Portugal and the loser at Vimeiro. Soult was the master of protracted attrition, pinning the allied army in Andalusia and Castile for nearly four years and still choosing to accept battle on the eve of Vitoria. Marmont's failure at Salamanca directly collapsed the entire French defensive line in the north. Wellington entered with the expeditionary force in the autumn of 1808, first saving the British army with a model withdrawal at Vimeiro and then using Beresford's Portuguese columns as his left wing and outpost, gradually turning defence into the offensive. His chief of staff George Murray, the engineer officer Bower and the cavalry commander Bentinck carried the allied logistics and mounted arm to a level that could support continuous operations. Another British figure of the first rank was John Moore, who turned a withdrawal into an attack at Corunna and was killed during the retreat; Barington led the storming columns at Badajoz, enduring one of the most brutal column attacks in the European experience of the British army. On the Spanish side, Castaños concentrated the army at Seville, Palafox held Zaragoza to the last, O'Donnell took Coruña and San Antonio, La Romana threw the French out of Menorca, and Espartero pursued them along the north-western front. The news that the Madrid rising of 2 to 6 May had been crushed travelled everywhere and left Ferdinand's credit with the nation all but exhausted. Among the guerrillas, Espoz y Mina ran a network across the Navarrese and Aragonese mountains, and El Empecinado led several hundred partidas that harried French columns around Guadalajara, carrying intelligence and metal across the ridges. And above all there was Napoleon himself, directing the war from the imperial centre and treating Spain as a secondary theatre for pinning down Britain; that misjudgement became the root of the whole war.
kits: 卡面上的是長槍：一六〇〇年前後歐洲方陣的冷兵器，鐵矛尖安在橡木長柄上，全長約二米半至三米，作用是在方陣前沿頂住衝鋒的騎兵，替身後的火槍隊撐出射擊空間。十八世紀中期以後，隨燧發火槍射程與射速的改善，長槍在歐洲線列作戰中全面退場；西班牙一八〇二年的步兵條例只列燧發滑膛槍與刺刀，線列營的紙面裝備裡已無長槍。戰爭開始時，長槍在伊比利亞退到榮譽與儀仗的層面：各家的具體記載頗有出入，較常見的說法是少數近衛與老字號營連仍以長槍作為旗幟與榮譽的標記，也有記述提到營連在集合、結陣時把長槍列在隊形前排。真正延續下來的是長矛方陣的思考方式：正面拒止、側翼迂迴，化成西班牙軍的拒止翼與方陣戰術，一八一一年阿爾布埃拉、一八一二年薩拉曼卡、一八一三年維多利亞的側翼反擊，都是這套邏輯的近代版。真正開火的武器是燧發滑膛槍：西班牙一八〇二年制式槍配刺刀，英軍舊制式步槍與一八〇二年後配發的貝克萊來福槍，法軍沙勒維爾制式步槍，葡軍沿用改裝過的舊式滑膛槍。砲兵方面，西班牙的聖巴巴拉砲兵制度下有四磅、六磅、八磅野戰砲與十二磅攻城砲，英軍為六磅、九磅野戰砲與皇家騎砲兵，法軍為格里博瓦爾制野戰砲，砲彈一律實心球形彈，攻城另用臼砲與科霍恩迫擊砲。攻城配套包括皇家工兵兵團的破城槓、木製防彈胸牆、坑道工具與排架，後勤靠牛拉的皇家後勤兵團大車隊與騾隊維持。游擊隊裝備多為自備，散彈槍、舊式長矛與自製手槍都有記載，另有以硫磺油脂製成的燃燒桶。英國皇家海軍的康格里夫火箭自軍艦與登陸灘頭發射，圍城時與攻城砲一同使用。
kitsEn: The card face shows a pike: the cold weapon of the European square in about 1600, an iron head on a long oak shaft, about two and a half to three metres in all, used at the front of the formation to hold back charging cavalry and open a firing space for the musketeers standing behind. After the middle of the eighteenth century, as flintlock muskets gained in range and rate of fire, the pike disappeared completely from line combat in Europe. The Spanish infantry ordinance of 1802 listed only flintlock muskets and bayonets, and no pike appeared any longer in the paper equipment of a line battalion. At the opening of the war the pike in Iberia had sunk to the level of honour and ceremony. The specific record is thin and the authorities differ, but the account most often repeated is that a few guards and old-established companies still carried pikes as a badge of rank and honour, and that companies kept them at the head of the column when forming up. What truly survived was the thinking behind the pike square: refuse the front, turn the flank, which hardened into the refused flank and the square in the Spanish army. The flank counterattacks at Albuera in 1811, Salamanca in 1812 and Vitoria in 1813 are all modern versions of that logic. The weapons that actually opened fire were flintlock muskets: the Spanish musket of 1802 with its bayonet, the older British service musket and the Baker rifle issued to rifle regiments after 1802, the French Charleville musket, and the modified old smoothbores still carried by the Portuguese. Artillery on the Spanish side ran on the Santa Bárbara system, with 4-, 6- and 8-pounder field pieces and 12-pounder siege guns; the British fielded 6- and 9-pounders and the Royal Horse Artillery; the French used Gribeauval ordnance. Shot was solid spherical throughout, with mortars and Coëhorn howitzers added for sieges. The siege train included the Royal Engineers' storming poles, timber blindage, mining tools and traversing racks, and supply was carried by the ox-drawn wagons of the Royal Logistic Corps and by mule teams. Guerrilla kit was largely self-provided: shotguns, old pikes and home-made pistols are all on record, together with fire-pots made of sulphur and grease. The Royal Navy's Congreve rockets were fired from ships and from the beaches, and used alongside siege guns when blockade was preferred to assault.
tactics: 法軍戰術是拿破崙戰爭的標準打法：師團縱隊行軍，敵前展開成橫線的攻擊縱隊分隊推進，梯次投入，靠密集炮兵與迂迴配合。一八一二年後改為軍團制，縱隊與後衛團之間拉得更長，一旦側翼被突破便成連鎖潰散。聯軍這邊相反，線列步兵排成兩三線橫陣，等敵進入百步至二百步射程才依序開火，射完退到後線裝填；英葡部隊以旅縱隊前進，每個縱隊由幾個營組成，營與營之間留出空隙，敵砲一來便散開成散兵線。威靈頓在北線多次主動放棄陣地，寧可退到後方縱深，讓法軍多走幾十里再把它拖進碎石坡與石橋的狹窄地形，這套以縱深換空間的做法在阿斯圖里亞斯與巴達霍斯戰線尤其明顯。西班牙軍的強項是守：據村莊、石牆與修道院設防，用拒止翼吸住法軍正面再以主力反擊側翼；缺點是紀律與配合差，縱隊與橫陣之間的轉換常在混亂中完成。葡軍旅縱隊在聯軍左翼作前哨，關鍵時刻插入法軍側後；游擊隊則不斷切斷通訊與糧道，迫使法軍分兵防守道路。圍城戰術上，聯軍多採封鎖代替突擊，一八一二年一月的羅德里戈城靠壕壘與炮火逼降，守軍三千五百餘人全員被俘，傷亡遠低於硬攻，一八一二年的巴達霍斯與一八一三年的巴約那、聖塞巴斯蒂安也循同一思路。海軍以登陸點、封鎖線與火箭砲支援陸上戰役，火箭在羅德里戈城與巴達霍斯攻城時都用過。
tacticsEn: French tactics were the standard Napoleonic pattern: divisional columns on the march, deployed on the enemy into attack columns that echeloned forward line by line, supported by massed batteries and turning movements. After 1812 the corps system stretched the distance between leading and trailing divisions, so a breach on one flank unravelled the rest in a chain. The allies did the opposite. Line infantry stood in two or three ranks, waited until the enemy came within a hundred to two hundred paces, and fired in succession, the rear rank stepping forward to reload. British and Portuguese formations advanced in brigade columns made of several battalions, with gaps between battalions, and scattered into skirmish order when French guns opened fire. In the northern theatre Wellington repeatedly surrendered ground, preferring to fall back into depth so that the French would be marched further before being caught on broken slopes and narrow stone bridges; this trade of depth for space is most visible along the Asturian and Badajoz lines. The Spanish army's strength was defence: it entrenched in villages, behind stone walls and in monasteries, used the refused flank to pin the French front and then struck the flank with the main body. Its weakness was discipline and mutual support, and the transition from column to line was often made in confusion. Portuguese brigades served as outposts on the allied left and could be thrown in against the French flank at the decisive moment, while the partidas cut communications and supply, forcing the French to spread out to guard roads. In siege work the allies usually preferred blockade to assault. Ciudad Rodrigo in January 1812 was reduced by trenches and gunfire until its garrison of some 3,500 surrendered almost intact, with far fewer casualties than a storm would have cost, and Badajoz in 1812 and Bayonne and San Sebastian in 1813 followed the same logic. The Royal Navy supported the land war with landing parties, blockading squadrons and rocket batteries, and rockets were used at the sieges of Ciudad Rodrigo and Badajoz.
data: 幾個有據可查的數字可以描出戰役的規模。一八〇七年十月入葡的法軍約二萬四千人，葡軍約三萬至四萬人，多數未經訓練即被解除武裝。一八〇八年三月西班牙可用野戰兵力約十萬，真正裝備齊全者不足三分之一，多數營僅有一半人齊裝。巴耶倫一役（一八〇八年七月）西軍與安達盧西亞民兵約一萬九千至二萬二千，對法軍杜邦師約八千人，法軍損失約二千人並有大批被俘。維梅羅一役英葡聯軍約八千人對法軍一萬四千人，法軍死傷約三千。科魯尼一役（一八〇九年一月）英軍約一萬六千人對紐伊部約二萬五千人，英軍陣亡約八百、負傷約一千五百。塔拉維拉一役（一八〇九年七月）英西聯軍約二萬五千對法軍約二萬二千，聯軍損失逾一千五百。圖德拉一役（一八〇九年十一月）法軍約一萬二千對西軍約八千。阿爾布埃拉一役（一八一一年五月）聯軍約二萬二千至二萬七千對法軍約二萬二千，十六日那天聯軍傷亡約六千，法軍約五千，後世稱之為英軍史上最慘烈的一日。薩拉曼卡一役（一八一二年七月）聯軍約五萬二千至六萬對法軍約四萬至五萬，法軍死傷約四五千、被俘約七千。維多利亞一役（一八一三年六月）聯軍約七萬二千對法軍約六萬五千，法軍傷亡約八千、被俘約一萬，包括法軍總監羅西耶爾在內，聯軍損失約五千。兵力此消彼長：英軍自一八〇八年的不足一萬增至一八一九年的九萬左右，葡軍由一萬上下增至五萬；法軍在半島的總損失各家估計由十五萬至二十五萬不等，西班牙軍損失估計逾二十萬，多屬傷病與逃亡。全戰線北起巴約那、南至直布羅陀，縱深近一千公里；一八〇八年九月西班牙中央軍團的強行軍，十日內推進約三百公里，幾乎耗盡全軍體力，卻是唯一一次把法軍逼出卡斯提爾的機會。
dataEn: A handful of documented figures convey the scale. In October 1807 the French force that entered Portugal numbered about 24,000, against a Portuguese army of 30,000 to 40,000, most of them untrained and disarmed as they were. In March 1808 Spain could field perhaps 100,000 men for operations, but fewer than a third were properly equipped, and many companies had half their men missing. At Bailén in July 1808 the Spanish army and the Andalusian militia numbered 19,000 to 22,000 against Dupont's division of about 8,000; the French lost some 2,000 and a mass surrendered. At Vimeiro roughly 8,000 British and Portuguese faced about 14,000 French, who lost around 3,000. At Corunna in January 1809 about 16,000 British faced Ney's 25,000, with British losses of some 800 killed and 1,500 wounded. At Talavera in July 1809 the British-Spanish army of about 25,000 met roughly 22,000 French, and the allies lost more than 1,500. At Tudela in November 1809 about 12,000 French opposed 8,000 Spaniards. At Albuera in May 1811 the allies fielded 22,000 to 27,000 against some 22,000 French; on the sixteenth the allies lost about 6,000 and the French about 5,000, and the day has been called the worst in the history of the British army. At Salamanca in July 1812 the allied 52,000 to 60,000 engaged 40,000 to 50,000 French, who lost 4,000 to 5,000 killed and wounded with some 7,000 captured. At Vitoria in June 1813 about 72,000 allies defeated 65,000 French, with 8,000 French casualties and 10,000 prisoners, including the French intendant Rossignol, while allied losses were around 5,000. Numbers shifted steadily across the war: the British army grew from fewer than 10,000 in 1808 to about 90,000 in 1813, and the Portuguese from around 10,000 to 50,000. French losses in the Peninsula are estimated at between 150,000 and 250,000, and Spanish losses at more than 200,000, mostly from sickness, wounds and desertion. The theatre stretched nearly a thousand kilometres from Bayonne to Gibraltar, and in September 1808 the central Spanish army marched some 300 kilometres in ten days, exhausting itself in the process, in the one attempt that pushed the French out of Castile.
cause: 一八〇七年之前，伊比利亞本來沒有戰事。是拿破崙的大陸封鎖體系把戰火帶進來的：一八〇五年特拉法加海戰之後，英國商船再不能自由進出歐洲港口，拿破崙轉而以俄羅斯、普魯士與奧地利施壓，想逼英國求和；一八〇七年提爾西特和約之後，他與俄國修好，轉而要求歐洲內陸國家一起封鎖英國。葡萄牙是最不肯低頭的一個，葡王若昂六世不願封閉本國港口，英國商船照樣入港避風。巴黎隨即策劃以入侵葡萄牙作為迫使葡國就範的手段，一八〇七年十月朱諾部由比斯開灣登陸，僅僅數週就攻入里斯本，葡王政府退往巴西。這個舉動激起了整個半島的連鎖反應：西班牙正與法國談判加入封鎖體系，卻在巴亞昂被拿破崙扣留國王斐迪南七世與王后，四月又在馬德里另立約瑟夫·波拿巴為西班牙國王；五月二日至六日馬德里民眾起義，起義被法軍鎮壓，消息傳到各地，安達盧西亞、卡斯提爾與巴斯克同日舉兵，戰爭由王位更迭擴大成全民抵抗。英國隨即以海上封鎖、貸款與遠征軍介入，卡斯楚雷加在政府層面拍板支援，威靈頓接管前線，於是西班牙的起義被壓成一場耗時六年的半島消耗戰。
causeEn: Before 1807 Iberia was not a battlefield. What carried the war there was Napoleon's continental system. After Trafalgar in 1805 British shipping could no longer move freely into European ports, and Napoleon turned instead on Russia, Prussia and Austria, trying to force Britain to terms. After Tilsit in 1807 he made peace with Russia and instead demanded that the continental powers join him in excluding British trade. Portugal was the one that refused to bow, for King John VI would not close Portuguese harbours and British ships simply sheltered there. Paris therefore planned an invasion of Portugal as the lever for bringing Lisbon to heel. In October 1807 Junot's corps landed in the Bay of Biscay and reached Lisbon within a matter of weeks, and the Portuguese royal government withdrew to Brazil. That move set off a chain reaction across the peninsula. Spain was negotiating to join the blockade when Ferdinand VII and his queen were detained at Bayonne, and in April Joseph Bonaparte was installed at Madrid as king of Spain. When the Madrid rising of 2 to 6 May was crushed by the French, the news spread, and Andalusia, Castile and the Basque provinces rose almost at once: a dispute over a crown had become a general rising. Britain then intervened with blockade, loans and an expeditionary force. Castlereagh committed the government at Westminster, and Wellington took over in the field, and the Spanish rising was compressed into a consuming war of attrition that would run for six years.
impact: 半島戰爭改變的不只是伊比利亞的版圖。第一，西班牙王國幾乎被戰爭掏空：常備軍在六年裡死傷、被俘、逃亡，一八一四年斐迪南七世回國時，軍隊在名冊上仍有十幾萬人，實際能拿起槍的不足十分之一，這批殘餘骨幹後來成為自由派軍官的來源，也讓西班牙此後十年陷於王位與立憲的反覆衝突。第二，它把拿破崙的帝國從一個歐洲強權拖成一具外強中乾的軀殼：法軍在西線牽制住英軍主力，本可投入德國戰役的兵力被釘在西班牙，拿破崙本人稱之為西班牙的潰瘍，一八一三年德國戰役失利、一八一四年第一次退位，源頭都在這片半島。第三，它催生了新的國家形態：一八一二年的加的斯議會在法軍圍城之中制訂憲法，確立君主立憲、代議制與民族語言權，成為西班牙現代國家的法律起點；同時，半島上持續的戰亂也讓美洲殖民地認定宗主國已無力保護它們，布宜諾斯艾利斯與蒙得維的亞在一八一〇至一八一二年間相繼脫離西班牙，南美洲的獨立從此走上不可逆的道路。第四，戰術層面，世界第一次看見常備軍與游擊隊、地面部隊與皇家海軍、聯盟多國指揮體系結合起來的完整形態；威靈頓自此被視為歐洲最會打仗的將軍之一，他從半島帶回來的經驗影響了此後二三十年的軍事教育，而西班牙的抵抗也讓人重新思考游擊戰與不對稱作戰的價值，百年後的理論家仍在討論它的示範作用。
impactEn: The Peninsular War changed far more than the map of Iberia. First, it hollowed out the Spanish kingdom. After six years of casualties, captures and desertions, the regular army still listed more than a hundred thousand men when Ferdinand VII returned in 1814, yet barely one in ten could actually shoulder a musket. The surviving cadre became a source of liberal officers and pushed Spain into a decade of recurring conflict over throne and constitution. Second, it drained the French empire of the strength that had made it the dominant power in Europe. The French army in the west tied down the main body of the British army, and the troops that might have gone to Germany were pinned in Spain; Napoleon himself called the peninsula his Spanish ulcer, and the German campaign of 1813 and the first abdication of 1814 both trace back to it. Third, the war produced a new form of state. The Cortes of Cádiz, sitting under siege, drew up a constitution in 1812 establishing constitutional monarchy, representation and the rights of the national language, and that instrument became the legal starting point of the modern Spanish state. At the same time, the endless fighting on the peninsula convinced the American colonies that the mother country could no longer protect them: Buenos Aires and Montevideo broke away between 1810 and 1812, and South American independence became irreversible. Fourth, at the level of tactics, the world saw for the first time a complete shape of combined operations: regular armies with partidas, land forces with the Royal Navy, and allied command structures drawn from several nations. Wellington was thereafter counted among the best soldiers in Europe, and the experience he carried home out of the peninsula shaped military education for the next two or three decades, while Spanish resistance forced a rethinking of guerrilla and asymmetric war that theorists were still debating a century later.
result: 一八一三年八月，最後的法軍要塞聖塞巴斯蒂安與巴約那先後開城，全線光復；一八一四年二月奧爾特茲一役，聯軍擊破克萊爾的法軍縱隊，二月底越過比爾多斯山；四月十日土魯斯一役，聯軍攻入城南，拿破崙的帝國在西線的最後一場會戰中被逐出伊比利亞。五月法軍全部撤出半島，戰爭以法國退出、西班牙與葡萄牙光復告終。聯軍付出的代價是幾萬人的傷亡與六年不斷的戰役消耗：英軍在半島的損失約四萬人，其中相當一部分是陣亡與重傷；維多利亞一役後法軍被俘的一萬人連同輜重被帶回，數百門砲與上千匹馬成了聯軍的戰利品。西班牙方面，斐迪南七世復位，他保留了英軍資助建立起來的常備軍框架，卻在一八一四年四月廢除加的斯憲法，把國家推回絕對王權，這一轉折讓西班牙在一八一四至一八二三年間經歷多次王位更替與自由派與專制派的正面衝突。威靈頓帶著葡軍與英軍的經驗回到英國，一年後出任首相；葡軍則保留了英軍的操典與一批英軍顧問，成為歐洲少數在戰後仍維持英式編制的軍隊。一八一四年四月拿破崙在巴黎的第一次退位，與半島這六年累積下來的消耗分不開。
resultEn: In August 1813 the last French strongholds, San Sebastian and Bayonne, opened their gates and the line was restored. At Orthez in February 1814 the allies broke Clausel's French columns and crossed the Pyrenees by the end of the month. At Toulouse on 10 April the allies stormed the southern approaches, and the last battle fought by Napoleon's empire in the west drove France out of Iberia. The French withdrew completely in May, and the war ended with their departure and the restoration of Spain and Portugal. The allies paid in tens of thousands of casualties and in six years of unbroken campaigning: British losses in the peninsula amount to some 40,000 men, a substantial share of them killed or severely wounded, and the 10,000 French prisoners taken after Vitoria were marched away with their baggage, several hundred guns and more than a thousand horses becoming allied trophies. In Spain, Ferdinand VII returned, kept the regular army framework that British money had built, and yet in April 1814 repealed the Cádiz constitution and pushed the country back into absolute monarchy; that reversal left Spain facing repeated changes of monarch and open clashes between liberals and absolutists between 1814 and 1823. Wellington carried the experience of the Portuguese and British armies home to Britain and became prime minister a year later. The Portuguese army kept British drill and a cadre of British advisers, becoming one of the few European armies to retain a British-style organisation after the war. Napoleon's first abdication at Paris in April 1814 cannot be separated from what those six years in Iberia had spent.
